title: Completeness of the six APN power families
summary: Determine whether the six known binary APN power-function families exhaust all APN power mappings up to CCZ equivalence.

formal_statement.body: For every positive integer $m$ and exponent $d$, suppose the power mapping $F_d(x)=x^d$ is almost perfect nonlinear on $\mathbb F_{2^m}$. Prove that $F_d$ is CCZ-equivalent to a member of one of the six known APN power families (Gold, Kasami, Welch, Niho, inverse, or Dobbertin), or exhibit an APN power mapping outside all six CCZ-equivalence families.

scope.domain: Almost perfect nonlinear power mappings over binary finite fields
assumptions: Classification is taken up to CCZ equivalence
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result proves the all-dimensions, all-exponents classification or gives an APN power mapping outside the six known CCZ families.

provenance.note: Dobbertin's 2001 primary text explicitly asks the table-completeness question, but a 2022 TIT restatement attributes the conjecture to his 1999 Niho-case paper. That 1999 primary text could not be inspected, so the earliest source remains unconfirmed.

progress.summary: Dobbertin's 2001 primary text explicitly asks whether the table of known APN power families is complete up to power-function equivalence.
The TIT paper restates Dobbertin's classification question and explains the matching CCZ-equivalence formulation for APN power functions.
The TIT paper states that the table of all known APN monomials is conjectured to be complete up to equivalence.
The TIT paper again records Dobbertin's conjecture that the known APN power families form a complete classification.
